title: Multi-Region Caching Strategies
description: Design multi-region caching architectures that minimize latency while maintaining data consistency across geographic locations.

data.text: Multi-region caching places Redis instances close to users in different geographic locations. The central challenge is balancing latency reduction against data consistency. Choosing the right replication strategy depends on your application's tolerance for stale reads versus its latency requirements.

In an active-passive setup, a single primary region handles all writes, and secondary regions replicate data asynchronously. In active-active (multi-master), each region accepts writes, requiring conflict resolution. Redis Enterprise supports active-active geo-replication with conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs), while open-source Redis requires careful application-level conflict handling.

data.title: Latency vs Consistency Trade-off
data.text: Users in Europe hitting a US primary will see ~100ms additional latency for writes. Active-passive replication reduces read latency but writes still go to the primary. Active-active removes the write latency penalty but introduces conflict resolution complexity.

data.text: In multi-region setups, routing reads to the nearest replica dramatically reduces latency. However, reads from replicas may be stale due to asynchronous replication. The staleness window depends on the replication link latency and throughput. Applications must accept eventual consistency for local reads or implement read-your-writes consistency by routing subsequent reads to the primary.

data.title: Multi-Region Cache Routing in Node.js

data.text: When the same key is modified in multiple regions, conflicts arise. Strategies include last-write-wins (using timestamps), version vectors, or application-specific merge logic. Redis Enterprise CRDTs provide automatic conflict resolution for common data types like counters and sets without application intervention.

cards.title: Strong Consistency
cards.description: All reads see the latest write, regardless of region.
cons: High write latency for distant users

cards.title: Eventual Consistency
cards.description: Writes propagate asynchronously; reads may be temporarily stale.

cards.title: Session Consistency
cards.description: A user always reads their own writes; other users may see stale data.

terms.definition: Asynchronous replication of data between Redis instances in different geographic regions.
Conflict-free Replicated Data Type — a data structure that can be replicated across nodes and merged automatically without conflicts.
A guarantee that a user will always see their own writes reflected in subsequent reads.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Multi-region caching reduces latency by placing replicas near users
Active-passive replication is simpler but all writes go to the primary
Active-active requires conflict resolution and is available in Redis Enterprise
Read-your-writes consistency requires routing subsequent reads to the primary region
data.takeaway: Choose your multi-region strategy based on your consistency requirements: caches can tolerate eventual consistency, while user session stores often need session consistency.
